reviewer: Codex author source review; independent approval pending

owner_creation.analysis: The num_metachars private c_int owns the number of initialized metacharacter bytes, zero initially and incremented after capacity selection.
owner_creation.invariant: The count describes initialized payload bytes only.
limitations: num_metachars counts payload bytes rather than owning their allocation.

aliases_escapes.analysis: add_metachar copies the old value into an index; the num_metachars count itself escapes only by value and retains no argument pointer.
aliases_escapes.invariant: Count metadata does not own the selected characters.
limitations: A count snapshot is meaningful only with its matching metachars pointer.

callback_targets.analysis: The num_metachars scalar selects data indices and never names an indirect call; strchr reads the resulting NUL string through metachars.
callback_targets.invariant: Payload length is not callback state.
limitations: The count supplies loop bounds but stores no callback target.

invalidation.analysis: The num_metachars count survives pointer replacement because strcpy preserves existing bytes, but it must still be bounded by the newly allocated extent.

mutation_commit.analysis: num_metachars+1 and the increment have no explicit overflow checks; byte and NUL writes follow those arithmetic results.
mutation_commit.invariant: Index arithmetic needs a checked capacity relationship.

release_pair.analysis: No free applies to the num_metachars count; retiring a string allocation must retire its logical count consistently, although the one-shot helper never resets this owner.
release_pair.invariant: Scalar cleanup cannot release the buffer itself.
limitations: Releasing metachars does not make a retained num_metachars value safe to use.

error_cleanup.analysis: malloc failure exits before num_metachars increments; arithmetic failure has no typed count/capacity rollback contract.
error_cleanup.invariant: Failed capacity growth must not publish a new count.

signals_handoff.analysis: num_metachars changes during one-shot parsing, but its type does not encode count-to-buffer validity for reuse or reentry.
signals_handoff.invariant: Current sequencing is a caller contract, not a safe type.
limitations: Current helper buffers remain raw C-shaped owners; unchecked growth/numeric arithmetic is recorded under M0-MEM-001, without claiming a demonstrated runtime failure.
